title: Why Students Tattle And How To End It
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin reframes tattling not as attention-seeking but as a symptom of poor classroom management, identifying three underlying causes: inconsistency (students no longer trust the teacher to enforce rules), inattention (a scrambling teacher who isn't observing closely enough), and confusion (unclear expectations about what actually breaks a rule). He argues that when students tattle, they're implicitly asking the teacher to fix a weakness in their own system rather than simply being needy. His recommended response is a simple, neutral acknowledgment — "Thanks for letting me know, I promise I'll take care of it" — followed by genuinely following through. He ties the fix back to core SCM principles: detailed modeling of the management plan, consistent enforcement, and vigilant observation, framing tattling's disappearance as a natural byproduct of shoring up those fundamentals.
